subject.title: fix: keep the global loop breaker reachable after tool blocks

question: Which representation should become the single canonical implementation for veto accounting in the loop detector: this PR’s explicit `loop-veto` outcome or the sentinel-hash approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109619?
rationale: Both branches address the same current-main defect with credible proof, but the persisted history contract and future extension point differ; selecting one is an agents-runtime ownership decision rather than a mechanical review correction.

options.title: Adopt the explicit outcome design
options.body: Land this branch after normal merge refresh because a named `loop-veto` discriminator keeps a semantic veto distinct from a hashed real tool result.

options.title: Adopt the sentinel-hash design
options.body: Choose https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109619 if maintainers prefer to avoid extending the diagnostic record shape, then close this competing branch.

options.title: Pause both candidates
options.body: Hold both PRs until the agents-runtime owner specifies the intended durable tool-history contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the explicit outcome design
recommendation.body: Land this branch after normal merge refresh because a named `loop-veto` discriminator keeps a semantic veto distinct from a hashed real tool result.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent module history shows direct ownership of configurable loop-detection behavior and its maintenance.
